svg.aria-label: Cold-weather heating: battery bank and water can
svg.text: Cold-weather heating: battery bank and water can
Snow camping (−5 to −15 °C nights): keep the LiFePO₄ bank above 0 °C so it may charge, stop every charger below +3 °C, and keep the 30 L can from freezing.

svg.text: NTC probe on the lid face, mid-height
Feed after QS1: opening QS1 for
storage also switches the heater off.
TH1: ON below +3 °C, OFF above +8 °C (probe on BT2,
Victron: DVCC on, shared temperature sense from
Ask iTechworld whether the BMS blocks charging
below 0 °C; the build doesn't rely on it.
~23 Ah on a −5 °C night, ~43–60 Ah at −10 to −15.
2 × 50 W warms a cold bank −10 → +5 °C in ~3–4 h.
Daily winter use is ~210 Ah of 800 Ah: plan
driving or shore power every 2–3 days.
Each pad has a normally-closed cut-out bonded
to it, in series: a stuck relay can't overheat
a battery case (50 °C) or the can (45 °C).
Pads only on the batteries' sides, between the
cage straps; never under a battery.
0.13 W/cm² on the case: confirm with iTechworld
that the case is fine at 50 °C locally.
1. Chill the TS1 lug (ice pack in a bag) below
+3 °C: every charger must stop or show 'low
2. Chill each probe: the relay must click on;
3. Warm each pad's cut-out with a heat gun:
